glos.a_ua.d: Average distance between the planet and its star, in Astronomical Units (1 AU = Earth-Sun distance). It changes over time due to tidal migration.
glos.B_gauss.d: Strength of the planetary magnetic field in Gauss. It is what shields the atmosphere from the stellar wind (magnetosphere).
glos.w_p.d: How fast the planet spins on its own axis, in radians per second. It changes due to stellar and lunar tides.
glos.e.d: How oval the orbit is. 0 = perfect circle; higher values = more elliptical orbit. It affects tidal heating.
glos.T_cmb_K.d: Temperature at the boundary between the planet's core and mantle, in Kelvin. It is one of the drivers of the thermal dynamo.
glos.B_gen_gauss.d: The part of the magnetic field that is actively generated by convection in the core (dynamo effect), instead of merely decaying.
glos.Rm.d: Measures whether the planet's core can sustain an active dynamo. Rm > 40 is considered the threshold for real field generation.
glos.M_atm_kg.d: How much atmosphere the planet has left, in kilograms. It drops over time through stellar-wind erosion if the magnetic field is weak.
glos.eps_deg.d: Tilt of the planet's rotation axis relative to its orbit, in degrees. Earth has ~23.4°.
glos.MHI.d: A score from 0 to 100 combining magnetic shielding, stable orbit, active field and moderate tidal heating, to estimate how favorable a planet's magnetic shield is.
glos.mhi_bruto.d: Sum of the 4 MHI components (shield, field, orbit, tide) before applying the extreme obliquity penalty.
glos.penalizacion_obl_pts.d: Points subtracted from the raw MHI when the planet's axial tilt is extreme, because it destabilizes the climate.
glos.categoria_mhi.d: Plain-words reading of the MHI score: 80+ High magnetic habitability · 50-79 Moderate / borderline habitability · <50 Sterile / exposed atmosphere.
glos.SIN_DATO.d: Explicit marker in the database: no real published measurement exists for that field. MHD-INT never invents a "reasonable" value in its place -- it leaves it marked like this.
glos.termico_estimado.d: Flag indicating that the planet's internal thermal parameters (core, mantle) do not come from a real source, but were estimated by planet category.
glos.eps_conocido.d: Flag that distinguishes an obliquity with real observational backing from an internal integrator value without that backing. When false, MHD-INT says so instead of showing a value as if it were measured.
glos.fuente_orbital.d: Indicates whether a planet's orbital data is "real" (measured), "estimated" or "revisar_pendiente" (pending review). It is the basis of the confidence Tier system.
glos.Tier_A_B_C.d: Classification of each planet by how well backed its data is: Tier A = real orbital and thermal data; Tier B = real orbital data but estimated thermal; Tier C = data to be reviewed.
